label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/xss): alert-TP — User input flows from request header -> param -> decoded param -> valuesList -> bar -> sql -> HTML response sink. The sink writes raw sql to the response without sanitizing the XSS payload. Alert 2 (java/sql-injection): alert-TP — Same flow leads to raw sql being passed to JDBC template execute(), allowing SQL injection. Both sinks receive attacker-controlled data.

evidence.note: User input captured from header and URL-decoded into param.
In doSomething, param added to list, list[0] removed, list[1] assigned to bar. Since list has 3 elements initially, removing index 0 leaves param at index 1. Thus bar = param.
SQL constructed using bar directly without escaping, enabling SQL injection.
Raw sql printed to HTML response, enabling XSS.
